property_summary: SetMinSum must revert if called before Initialized when the parameter is non-zero
If SetMinSum succeeds (does not revert), then the passed _val must be zero.

The value of c.MinSum() must equal the last value passed to SetMinSum before Initialized was called; the buggy version leaves MinSum at zero, causing Collect to require balances >= 0 instead of the intended threshold.

After initialization, c.MinSum() must be invariant across a call to Collect(...) that does not revert; the buggy version's Collect may allow unexpected state transitions that violate this invariant when MinSum remains zero.

After initialization and a successful non-reverting Collect, c.MinSum() must equal the value set before initialization; the buggy version leaves MinSum permanently zero, violating this equality once MinSum was set to non-zero.

If MinSum was set to a non-zero value before initialization, then a successful Collect that would be blocked by that threshold should revert in the reference but succeeds in the buggy version, changing MinSum from a decidable invariant to an observable difference in call success.

After initialization, if MinSum was set to a non-zero value, then a call to Collect with _am > 0 that does not revert must leave MinSum unchanged; the buggy version never sets MinSum, so it stays zero, violating this post-condition when the set value was non-zero.
SetMinSum should revert when called before initialization, but succeed after initialization.
SetMinSum reverts if and only if the contract is initialized.
SetMinSum never reverts if the contract has not been initialized.
